payload.claim: `_reclaim_build_cache()` (line 2425) now runs, and can block for up to `RECLAIM_BUILD_CACHE_TIMEOUT_S` = 600s, before `datetime.now()` is read to resolve `--until` on line 2429. `_resolve_until` treats a time no later than `now` as having already passed and rolls it to tomorrow (its own docstring, saffron/cli.py:2186-2189). If the reclaim's duration straddles the operator's `--until` clock time (plausible on a slow host, which is exactly the case the 600s bound was sized for), `now()` is read after that moment has passed and the whole night's deadline silently rolls forward 24 hours instead of stopping at the intended time. This is new: before this diff `datetime.now()` was read immediately after the unattended refusal with no delay in between, so the window in which this boundary could be crossed was negligible; this change widens it to the length of a real subprocess call. No test exercises an `--until` value that falls inside the reclaim's run time, so the gates do not see it.
